title: Asiana 214: The Autothrottle Was in HOLD — What the NTSB Found (San Francisco, 2013)
description:
July 6, 2013, San Francisco International Airport: Asiana Airlines flight 214, a Boeing 777-200ER, descends below the visual glidepath on its approach to runway 28L and strikes the seawall. Explained second by second, only with the NTSB final report NTSB/AAR-14/01: flight data, cockpit voice recorder (in NTSB translation), and the board's findings.

The NTSB determined that the probable cause was the flight crew's mismanagement of the airplane's descent during the visual approach, the pilot flying's unintended deactivation of automatic airspeed control, the flight crew's inadequate monitoring of airspeed, and the flight crew's delayed execution of a go-around after they became aware that the airplane was below acceptable glidepath and airspeed tolerances. Contributing factors listed by the NTSB include the complexities of the autothrottle and autopilot flight director systems, which were inadequately described in Boeing's documentation and Asiana's pilot training, and flight crew fatigue.
